english: Here, indeed, there are six hundred purgatives (virecana); six supports of purgation; five sources (yoni) of kaṣāya; a fivefold preparation of kaṣāya; fifty great kaṣāyas; and five hundred kaṣāyas. This is the summary.

hindi: 'छह सौ विरेचन' ऐसा जो कहा गया, उसे यहाँ संक्षेप में उदाहृत करके हम कल्पोपनिषद् में विस्तार से समझाएँगे। उनमें फलों में एक सौ तैंतीस योग बताए गए हैं; जीमूतक में उनतालीस योग हैं; इक्ष्वाकु में पैंतालीस; धामार्गव योगों से युक्त होकर साठ प्रकार का होता है; कुटज अठारह प्रकार से योग को प्राप्त होता है; कृतवेधन योगों से युक्त होकर साठ प्रकार का होता है; श्यामा और त्रिवृत् के सौ योग बताए गए हैं, और यहाँ दस अन्य योग और होते हैं; चतुरङ्गुल बारह प्रकार से योग को प्राप्त होता है; लोध्र विधि में सोलह योगों से युक्त है; महावृक्ष बीस योगों से युक्त होता है; सप्तला और शङ्खिनी के उनतालीस योग हैं; दन्ती और द्रवन्ती के अड़तालीस; इस प्रकार (ये) छह सौ विरेचन (हुए)।
english: 'Six hundred purgatives' -- what was said thus, we shall cite here in summary and expound in detail in the Kalpa-upaniṣad. Among these: among fruits a hundred and thirty-three (read: thirty-three plus a hundred) formulations (yoga) are set forth; among jīmūtaka there are thirty-nine formulations; among ikṣvāku forty-five; dhāmārgava, joined with formulations, becomes sixty-fold; kuṭaja enters into formulation eighteen ways; kṛtavedhana, joined with formulations, becomes sixty-fold; a hundred formulations of śyāmā and trivṛt are set forth, and here there are ten other formulations; caturaṅgula enters into formulation twelve ways; lodhra, in the procedure, is joined with sixteen formulations; mahāvṛkṣa is joined with twenty formulations; there are thirty-nine formulations of saptalā and śaṅkhinī; forty-eight of dantī and dravantī. Thus (these are) the six hundred purgatives.
notes: (1) The stray '&' mentioned in the tool flag is not visible in the given text; I could not tell where it was, so the word division is taken as printed. (2) 'trayastriṃśad-yoga-śatam' is literally 'thirty-three (and) a hundred formulations'; 133 is chosen because only it makes the sum 600 (checked), not on the grammar alone; 3300 would break the total: with 39+45+60+18+60+110+12+16+20+39+48 the total is exactly 600 only if the fruits give 133 (133+39=172, +45=217, +60=277, +18=295, +60=355, +110=465, +12=477, +16=493, +20=513, +39=552, +48=600). The 110 comes from 'śyāmā-trivṛt-yoga-śatam' plus 'daśa apare'. (3) 'kalpopaniṣadi' is rendered literally as 'in the Kalpa-upaniṣad'; the text does not say here which section is meant. (4) 'vidhau' (loc. sg., 'in the procedure/rule') is vague; it may also be read as 'in the (purgative) method'. (5) In 'aṣṭacatvāriṃśad dantī-dravantyoḥ' the word yogāḥ is understood from the preceding clause; same for 'pañcacatvāriṃśad ikṣvākuṣu'. (6) 'phaleṣu' is plural: 'among fruits' (the set of fruit drugs, not named here). (7) 'iti yad uktam' refers back to unit 3 / the heading 'ṣaḍ virecanaśatāni'.
lines_iast: ṣaḍ virecanaśatāni, iti yaduktaṃ tadiha saṃgraheṇodāhṛtya vistareṇa kalpopaniṣadi vyākhyāsyāmaḥ; tatra trayastriṃśadyogaśataṃ praṇītaṃ phaleṣu, ekonacatvāriṃśajjīmūtakeṣu yogāḥ, pañcacatvāriṃśadikṣvākuṣu, dhāmārgavaḥ ṣaṣṭidhā bhavati yogayuktaḥ, kuṭajastvaṣṭādaśadhā yogameti, kṛtavedhanaṃ ṣaṣṭidhā bhavati yogayuktaṃ, śyāmātrivṛdyogaśataṃ praṇītaṃ daśāpare cātra bhavanti yogāḥ, caturaṅgulo dvādaśadhā yogameti, lodhraṃ vidhau ṣoḍaśayogayuktaṃ, mahāvṛkṣo bhavati viṃśatiyogayuktaḥ, ekonacatvāriṃśat saptalāśaṅkhinyoryogāḥ, aṣṭacatvāriṃśaddantīdravantyoḥ, iti ṣaḍvirecanaśatāni

english: 'The fifty great kaṣāyas' -- what was said thus, we shall now expound further; namely: jīvanīya (life-giving), bṛṃhaṇīya (bulk-promoting), lekhanīya (scraping), bhedanīya (splitting, breaking up), sandhānīya (joining, uniting), dīpanīya (kindling digestion) -- this is a kaṣāya-class (kaṣāya-varga) of six; balya (strength-related), varṇya (complexion-related), kaṇṭhya (throat-related), hṛdya (heart-related) -- a kaṣāya-class of four; tṛptighna (satiety-removing), arśoghna (piles-removing), kuṣṭhaghna (kuṣṭha-removing), kaṇḍūghna (itching-removing), krimighna (worm-removing), viṣaghna (poison-removing) -- a kaṣāya-class of six; english: Namely: jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, jīvantī and madhuka — these are the ten life-giving (jīvanīya) drugs. notes: Group counts: G1 [snehopaga]: mṛdvīkā / madhuka / madhu-parṇī / medā / vidārī / kākolī / kṣīra-kākolī / jīvaka / jīvantī / śāla-parṇī (10); G2 [svedopaga]: śobhāñjanaka / eraṇḍa / arka / vṛścīra / punarnavā / yava / tila / kulattha / māṣa / badara (10); G3 [vamanopaga]: madhu / madhuka / kovidāra / karbudāra / nīpa / vidula / bimbī / śaṇapuṣpī / sadā-puṣpā / pratyak-puṣpā (10); G4 [virecanopaga]: drākṣā / kāśmarya / parūṣaka / abhayā / āmalaka / bibhītaka / kuvala / badara / karkandhu / pīlu (10); G5 [āsthāpanopaga]: trivṛt / bilva / pippalī / kuṣṭha / sarṣapa / vacā / vatsaka-phala / śata-puṣpā / madhuka / madana-phala (10); G6 [anuvāsanopaga]: rāsnā / sura-dāru / bilva / madana / śata-puṣpā / vṛścīra / punarnavā / śva-daṃṣṭrā / agni-mantha / śyonāka (10); G7 [śirovirecanopaga]: jyotiṣmatī / kṣavaka / marica / pippalī / viḍaṅga / śigru / sarṣapa / apāmārga-taṇḍula / śvetā / mahā-śvetā (10). Notes: (1) kṣīrakālolī read as kṣīra-kākolī (see text_flags); with the correction the group is ten, but note kākolī and kṣīra-kākolī both occur. (2) Group 3 begins with "madhu" and "madhuka" as two names; the glosses do not identify them. (3) śobhāñjanakairaṇḍārka = śobhāñjanaka + eraṇḍa + arka (a+e -> ai; a+a -> ā); an alternative division śobhāñjana + kairaṇḍa is not used. (4) Group 5 and 6 use compound names vatsaka-phala, madana-phala, apāmārga-taṇḍula, which are treated as single names (their parts would otherwise make the count exceed ten). (5) -upaga class names are rendered literally as "adjunct to / going along with" the named treatment; āsthāpana is the decoction enema (a form of basti) and anuvāsana the oil enema; these glosses are standard, not drawn from the verse. (6) Final "iti saptakaḥ kaṣāyavargaḥ" = closing formula "thus the sevenfold class".

hindi: जम्बू, आम्र-पल्लव, मातुलुंग, अम्ल-बदर, दाडिम, यव, षष्टिक, उशीर, मृत्तिका (मिट्टी) और लाज — ये दस वमन को रोकने वाले (छर्दिनिग्रहण) हैं। नागर, धन्वयवासक, मुस्त, पर्पटक, चन्दन, किराततिक्त, गुडूची, ह्रीवेर, धान्यक और पटोल — ये दस तृष्णा को रोकने वाले (तृष्णानिग्रहण) हैं। शटी, पुष्करमूल, बदरबीज, कण्टकारिका, बृहती, वृक्षरुहा, अभया, पिप्पली, दुरालभा और कुलीरशृंगी — ये दस हिक्का को रोकने वाले (हिक्कानिग्रहण) हैं। इस प्रकार यह तीन का कषायवर्ग है।
english: Jambū, āmra-pallava, mātuluṅga, amla-badara, dāḍima, yava, ṣaṣṭika, uśīra, mṛd (clay) and lāja: these are the ten vomiting-checking ones (chardi-nigrahaṇa). Nāgara, dhanvayavāsaka, musta, parpaṭaka, candana, kirāta-tikta, guḍūcī, hrīvera, dhānyaka and paṭola: these are the ten thirst-checking ones (tṛṣṇā-nigrahaṇa). Śaṭī, puṣkara-mūla, badara-bīja, kaṇṭakārikā, bṛhatī, vṛkṣaruhā, abhayā, pippalī, durālabhā and kulīra-śṛṅgī: these are the ten hiccup-checking ones (hikkā-nigrahaṇa). Thus the triad of kaṣāya-vargas.

hindi: प्रियंगु, अनन्ता, आम्र-अस्थि (आम की गुठली), कट्वंग, लोध्र, मोचरस, समंगा, धातकी के फूल, पद्मा और पद्मकेशर — ये दस मल को बाँधने वाले (पुरीषसंग्रहणीय) हैं। जम्बू, शल्लकी, त्वक् (छाल), कच्छुरा, मधूक, शाल्मली, श्रीवेष्टक, भुनी हुई मिट्टी, पयस्या, उत्पल और तिलकणा — ये दस मल को शुद्ध करने वाले (पुरीषविरजनीय) हैं। जम्बू, आम्र, प्लक्ष, वट, कपीतन, उदुम्बर, अश्वत्थ, भल्लातक, अश्मन्तक और सोमवल्क — ये दस मूत्र को बाँधने वाले (मूत्रसंग्रहणीय) हैं। पद्म, उत्पल, नलिन, कुमुद, सौगन्धिक, पुण्डरीक, शतपत्र, मधुक, प्रियंगु और धातकी के फूल — ये दस मूत्र को शुद्ध करने वाले (मूत्रविरजनीय) हैं। वृक्षादनी, श्वदंष्ट्रा, वसुक, वशिर, पाषाणभेद, दर्भ, कुश, काश, गुन्द्र और इत्कट की जड़ें — ये दस मूत्र का विरेचन करने वाले (मूत्रविरेचनीय) हैं। इस प्रकार यह पाँच का कषायवर्ग है।
english: Priyaṅgu, anantā, āmra-asthi (mango-stone), kaṭvaṅga, lodhra, mocarasa, samaṅgā, dhātakī-flowers, padmā and padma-keśara: these are the ten faeces-binding ones (purīṣa-saṃgrahaṇīya). Jambū, śallakī, tvak (bark), kacchurā, madhūka, śālmalī, śrīveṣṭaka, bhṛṣṭa-mṛt (roasted clay), payasyā, utpala and tila-kaṇā: these are the ten faeces-cleansing ones (purīṣa-virajanīya). Jambū, āmra, plakṣa, vaṭa, kapītana, udumbara, aśvattha, bhallātaka, aśmantaka and soma-valka: these are the ten urine-binding ones (mūtra-saṃgrahaṇīya). Padma, utpala, nalina, kumuda, saugandhika, puṇḍarīka, śatapatra, madhuka, priyaṅgu and dhātakī-flowers: these are the ten urine-cleansing ones (mūtra-virajanīya). Vṛkṣādanī, śvadaṃṣṭrā, vasuka, vaśira, pāṣāṇa-bheda, darbha, kuśa, kāśa, gundra and itkaṭa-roots: these are the ten urine-purging ones (mūtra-virecanīya). Thus the group of five kaṣāya-vargas.

Group 2 (purīṣa-virajanīya): token 'jambuśallakītvakkacchurāmadhūkaśālmalīśrīveṣṭakabhṛṣṭamṛtpayasyotpalatilakaṇā' is an unresolved BOUNDARY/TEXT DOUBT. As literally split the token has 11 names (jambū, śallakī, tvak, kacchurā, madhūka, śālmalī, śrīveṣṭaka, bhṛṣṭa-mṛt, payasyā, utpala, tila-kaṇā); it is ten only if tvak is taken with śallakī (śallakī-tvak) or distributed over jambū and śallakī; it is 12 if tila and kaṇā are also separate. The translation lists all the items as split and states 'ten' as the Sanskrit does. Group 3 (mūtra-saṃgrahaṇīya): 1 jambū, 2 āmra, 3 plakṣa, 4 vaṭa, 5 kapītana, 6 udumbara, 7 aśvattha, 8 bhallātaka, 9 aśmantaka, 10 soma-valka = 10. Group 4 (mūtra-virajanīya): 1 padma, 2 utpala, 3 nalina, 4 kumuda, 5 saugandhika, 6 puṇḍarīka, 7 śatapatra, 8 madhuka, 9 priyaṅgu, 10 dhātakī-puṣpa = 10. Group 5 (mūtra-virecanīya): 1 vṛkṣādanī, 2 śvadaṃṣṭrā, 3 vasuka, 4 vaśira, 5 pāṣāṇa-bheda, 6 darbha, 7 kuśa, 8 kāśa, 9 gundra, 10 itkaṭa-mūla = 10. Group names: virajanīya taken as 'cleansing/purifying' (vi-√rañj, literally 'de-colouring'); the exact sense is not stated in the Sanskrit. saṃgrahaṇīya = 'binding/holding together'.

hindi: द्राक्षा, अभया, आमलक, पिप्पली, दुरालभा, शृंगी, कण्टकारिका, वृश्चीर, पुनर्नवा और तामलकी — ये दस कास को हरने वाले (कासहर) हैं। शटी, पुष्करमूल, अम्लवेतस, एला, हिंगु, अगुरु, सुरसा, तामलकी, जीवन्ती और चण्डा — ये दस श्वास को हरने वाले (श्वासहर) हैं। पाटला, अग्निमन्थ, श्योनाक, बिल्व, काश्मर्य, कण्टकारिका, बृहती, शालपर्णी, पृश्निपर्णी और गोक्षुरक — ये दस शोथ को हरने वाले (श्वयथुहर) हैं। सारिवा, शर्करा, पाठा, मंजिष्ठा, द्राक्षा, पीलु, परूषक, अभया, आमलक और बिभीतक — ये दस ज्वर को हरने वाले (ज्वरहर) हैं। द्राक्षा, खर्जूर, प्रियाल, बदर, दाडिम, फल्गु, परुषक, इक्षु, यव और षष्टिका — ये दस श्रम (थकान) को हरने वाले (श्रमहर) हैं। इस प्रकार यह पाँच का कषायवर्ग है।
english: Drākṣā, abhayā, āmalaka, pippalī, durālabhā, śṛṅgī, kaṇṭakārikā, vṛścīra, punarnavā and tāmalakī: these are the ten cough-removing ones (kāsa-hara). Śaṭī, puṣkara-mūla, amla-vetasa, elā, hiṅgu, aguru, surasā, tāmalakī, jīvantī and caṇḍā: these are the ten breathlessness-removing ones (śvāsa-hara). lines_iast: nahi vistarasya pramāṇamasti, na cāpyatisaṃkṣepo 'lpabuddhīnāṃ sāmarthyāyopakalpate, tasmādanatisaṃkṣepeṇānativistareṇa copadiṣṭāḥ
lines_deva: नहि विस्तरस्य प्रमाणमस्ति, न चाप्यतिसंक्षेपो ऽल्पबुद्धीनां सामर्थ्यायोपकल्पते, तस्मादनतिसंक्षेपेणानतिविस्तरेण चोपदिष्टाः

hindi: ऐसा कहने वाले भगवान् आत्रेय से अग्निवेश ने कहा — भगवन्! ये पाँच सौ कषाय पूरे नहीं होते, क्योंकि उन-उन महाकषायों में वे-वे ही अङ्ग (अवयव) बार-बार आ जाते हैं।
english: To the venerable Ātreya, who spoke thus, Agniveśa said: Venerable sir, these five hundred kaṣāyas are not completed (filled up), for those very same members (aṅga) recur in those various great kaṣāyas.

english: The venerable Ātreya said to him: Agniveśa, an intelligent person should not look at this in this way.

lines_deva: तमुवाच भगवानात्रेयः --- नैतदेवं बुद्धिमता द्रष्टव्यमग्निवेश

hindi: जिस (स्रोत) से, जितने और जिन द्रव्यों से छह सौ विरेचन यहाँ संक्षेप में कहे गए हैं, और उसी प्रकार इनके छह आश्रय भी (कहे गए हैं)।
english: From which (source), as many as, and by which substances (dravya), six hundred purgatives (virecana) have been stated here in brief, and likewise their six bases.
notes: 'yataḥ' could also mean 'because'; here taken as 'from which (source)', parallel to 'yāvanti' and 'yaiḥ dravyaiḥ'. 'ṣaḍāśrayāḥ' (six bases) is left uninterpreted. 'uktāni' is neuter plural, agreeing with 'virecana-śatāni'; the phrase is read as 'six hundred purgatives (arising) from which source, in what number and with which drugs'. Syllable count 16+16, fits anuṣṭubh.
lead_in_english: Here are the verses on this.
lines_iast: yato yāvanti yairdravyairvirecanaśatāni ṣaṭ
uktāni saṃgraheṇeha tathaivaiṣāṃ ṣaḍāśrayāḥ
lines_deva: यतो यावन्ति यैर्द्रव्यैर्विरेचनशतानि षट्
उक्तानि संग्रहेणेह तथैवैषां षडाश्रयाः

hindi: लवण को छोड़कर रस भी 'कषाय' नाम से कहे गए हैं; इसलिए कषायों की योनि (उत्पत्ति-स्रोत) पाँच प्रकार की बताई गई है।
english: The tastes (rasa) excluding salt (lavaṇa) are also termed 'kaṣāya'; therefore the source (yoni) of the kaṣāyas is declared to be fivefold.
notes: Source flag: a stray '&' was removed by the tool in this unit; the tokens as given scan correctly (16+16) and read sensibly, so no word-division problem is evident. 'lavaṇavarjyāḥ' is taken as 'having salt excluded'. 'Kaṣāya' here is the class-name (not the astringent taste alone).
lines_iast: rasā lavaṇavarjyāśca kaṣāya iti saṃjñitāḥ
tasmāt pañcavidhā yoniḥ kaṣāyāṇāmudāhṛtā
lines_deva: रसा लवणवर्ज्याश्च कषाय इति संज्ञिताः
तस्मात् पञ्चविधा योनिः कषायाणामुदाहृता

hindi: उसी प्रकार इनकी कल्पना (तैयार करने की विधि) भी फिर पाँच प्रकार की कही गई है; और महान् कषायों के पचास (वर्ग) बताए गए हैं।
english: Likewise, the preparation (kalpana) of these has again been stated as fivefold; and fifty of the great kaṣāyas have been enumerated.
notes: 'kalpana' is rendered 'preparation' (the five preparations are not named in this unit). 'punaḥ' could also be read as 'further'.
lines_iast: tathā kalpanamapyeṣāmuktaṃ pañcavidhaṃ punaḥ
mahatāṃ ca kaṣāyāṇāṃ pañcāśat parikīrtitā
lines_deva: तथा कल्पनमप्येषामुक्तं पञ्चविधं पुनः
महतां च कषायाणां पञ्चाशत् परिकीर्तिता

hindi: और भी कषायों के पाँच सौ (वर्ग) भाग-भाग करके, लक्षण के लिए कहे गए हैं; क्योंकि विस्तार की कोई सीमा नहीं मिलती।
english: And also five hundred (classes) of kaṣāyas have been stated, part by part, for the purpose of characterization; for there is no limit to elaboration.
notes: 'bhāgaśaḥ' may also be rendered 'in divisions/sections'. Syllable count 16+16.
lines_iast: pañca cāpi kaṣāyāṇāṃ śatānyuktāni bhāgaśaḥ
lakṣaṇārthaṃ, pramāṇaṃ hi vistarasya na vidyate
lines_deva: पञ्च चापि कषायाणां शतान्युक्तानि भागशः
लक्षणार्थं, प्रमाणं हि विस्तरस्य न विद्यते

words.gram: m. nom. sg.; compound analysis doubtful

hindi: और अत्यन्त संक्षेप भी सामर्थ्य के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं होता; इसलिए अल्पबुद्धि वाले के लिए यह (वर्णन) न अति संक्षिप्त है और न अति विस्तृत।
english: Nor does excessive brevity suffice to serve capability; therefore, for one of little intelligence, this (exposition) is neither too brief nor too elaborate.
notes: Two points of doubt. (1) 'alam' with 'na' is taken as 'does not suffice'; (2) 'nātisaṃkṣepavistaraḥ' is taken as na + ati-saṃkṣepa-vistara (excess of brevity/elaboration; the compound analysis, a masc. sg. dvandva with ati, is doubtful) ('not too brief and not too elaborate'), parallel to prose unit 20 ('anatisaṃkṣepeṇānativistareṇa'). The subject of 'ayam' (this exposition) is understood. 'alpabuddheḥ' is a genitive singular, understood as 'for one of little intelligence'.
lines_iast: na cālamatisaṃkṣepaḥ sāmarthyāyopakalpate
alpabuddherayaṃ tasmānnātisaṃkṣepavistaraḥ
lines_deva: न चालमतिसंक्षेपः सामर्थ्यायोपकल्पते
अल्पबुद्धेरयं तस्मान्नातिसंक्षेपविस्तरः

hindi: मन्द (धीमे) लोगों के व्यवहार के लिए और बुद्धिमानों की बुद्धि की वृद्धि के लिए, क्योंकि कषायों का यह पचास का वर्ग कहा गया है।
english: For the practical use of the dull and for the growth of the intellect of the wise; for this group of fifty kaṣāyas has been set forth.
notes: 'mandānām' is taken as 'of the dull/slow (in understanding)'; 'vyavahāra' as 'practical use, handling'. 'hi' is explanatory/emphatic.
lines_iast: mandānāṃ vyavahārāya, budhānāṃ buddhivṛddhaye
pañcāśatko hyayaṃ vargaḥ kaṣāyāṇāmudāhṛtaḥ
lines_deva: मन्दानां व्यवहाराय, बुधानां बुद्धिवृद्धये
पञ्चाशत्को ह्ययं वर्गः कषायाणामुदाहृतः

hindi: जो उन (कषायों) के बाह्य और आभ्यन्तर कर्मों में योग (उपयोग), संयोग (मेल) और प्रयोग को जानता है, वह श्रेष्ठ वैद्य है।
english: He who knows, in the external and internal actions (karma) of these, their application (yoga), combination (saṃyoga) and administration (prayoga), is the best of physicians.
notes: Word order: 'yogam' is taken with both 'bāhyeṣu karmasu' and 'ābhyantareṣu (karmasu)'. The exact distinction between yoga, saṃyoga and prayoga is left as the plain senses given; commentators may differ. 'bhiṣagvaraḥ' could also be 'excellent physician'.
lines_iast: teṣāṃ karmasu bāhyeṣu yogamābhyantareṣu ca
saṃyogaṃ ca prayogaṃ ca yo veda sa bhiṣagvaraḥ
lines_deva: तेषां कर्मसु बाह्येषु योगमाभ्यन्तरेषु च
संयोगं च प्रयोगं च यो वेद स भिषग्वरः
